ctx.x: Yeah, he mentioned Jack Pettis. He liked Jack Pettis.

MR. CHALLIS: So did Donald Murray. Well, so the band had those arrangements, but actually for nice tunes, pop tunes, they didn't have too many, and they were interested -- the band had always felt that it hadn't had any hits, recorded hits so they were sort of -- I was sort of lying back until they got the arrangements. They went down to New York and they were going to get the tunes to do and that would give me about a week or two weeks, ten days, something like that, to work on some of the tunes.

One of the first things, he says, he asked me, 'Do you score?' I thought, 'What the hell's he talking about? Asking me. Score, you get score paper, and you write it down,' and he explained it to me and I said, 'Oh, I just write out the parts and that's it.' So 'Well, we'll have to get you some score paper' and I didn't know too much and it's naive or stupid to say that. But at that time, I hadn't scored, I didn't know what scoring was all about. The only way to make an arrangement, I thought, was write out the…
